title: Trafficking Victims Prevention and Protection Reauthorization Act of 2022
official_summary:
Trafficking Victims Prevention and Protection Reauthorization Act of 2022

This bill reauthorizes, updates, and expands federal efforts to address domestic trafficking, including to make permanent the U.S. Advisory Council on Human Trafficking and reauthorize various grants, activities, and programs that support victims of domestic trafficking.

summary.headline: A 2023 law renews and expands federal programs that address domestic human trafficking and support its victims.
summary.what_it_does: The law reauthorizes federal efforts to address domestic trafficking, which means it extends programs that were set to run under earlier authority. It makes the U.S. Advisory Council on Human Trafficking permanent. It also reauthorizes various grants, activities, and programs that support victims of domestic trafficking.

who_it_affects.how: Programs and grants that provide support to victims of domestic trafficking are renewed under the law.

who_it_affects.group: Organizations that receive federal grants to serve trafficking survivors
who_it_affects.how: Federal grant programs that fund victim support work are reauthorized, so these groups can continue to apply for and receive that funding.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the U.S. Advisory Council on Human Trafficking
who_it_affects.how: The council no longer depends on a set end date because the law makes it permanent.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on January 5, 2023. The summary does not list separate start dates for individual provisions.
